version.philosophy: An applied migration is history. Databases in the field were built from it, so it must never change; every schema change is a new, forward-only migration that preserves existing records.
version.method: Add the next numbered migration, apply it to a copy of a real database, prove that existing records read back unchanged, and refuse to run against schemas newer than the code understands.

inputs.change: The schema change required and the behaviour that needs it.
inputs.database_copy: A copy of a representative existing database file.

outputs.migration: One new migration file with the next sequence number.
outputs.evidence: Test output showing that existing records survive the migration unchanged.

preconditions: No applied migration file is modified.
postconditions: The schema version advances by exactly one per new migration.
Records written before the migration read back byte-for-byte identical.

steps.action: Read the existing migrations and the record contract the change affects.
Add NNNN_<name>.sql with the next number; never edit an earlier file.
Add a test that opens a database created before the change and reads existing records back.
Run the migration against a copy of a real database file and compare record reads before and after.
Update the record contract documentation and note compatibility consequences for older binaries.
